proposals.relationship: Adams criticizes Sioui’s emphasis on guilt and moral reconciliation for inadequately addressing the economic and political structures of colonial domination (1992).
proposals.evidence_note: A specific argument in Adams’s review of the English translation, credited to Sheila Fischman. He also finds the Sacred Circle discussion useful. The atlas records his criticism without adopting his separate epidemiological assertions or his judgment of who possesses an Aboriginal consciousness; Sioui’s whole book remains unread.
primary_locators: Native Studies Review 8.2 (1992), pp. 143–146, especially p. 144 final paragraphs, p. 145 first two paragraphs and p. 146 conclusion.

proposals.relationship: Dickason questions Sioui’s presentation of Lahontan as the first European to appreciate Indigenous thought, pointing to the earlier Las Casas while urging respectful attention to Sioui’s argument (1992).
proposals.evidence_note: The review discusses both Trigger and Sioui; only its Sioui-specific passage supports this relationship. This is a bounded correction within an appreciative reception, not wholesale rejection of autohistory. The reviewed French original is dated 1989; the English translation is a separate 1992 manifestation.
primary_locators: Revue française d’histoire d’outre-mer 79.295 (1992), p. 285, final two paragraphs; conclusion continues p. 286.

proposals.relationship: Sioui recalls that Lévi-Strauss read and endorsed his work after Pierre Maranda passed it on, providing encouragement during his return to university.
proposals.evidence_note: Reported in Sioui’s 2013 interview with Katie Hyslop. Maranda retains the mediating role; the underlying letter or manuscript was not obtained, and the recollection does not establish formal supervision, structuralist influence, or endorsement of every historical claim. No precise date for the earlier exchange is invented.
primary_locators: “Rewriting history” section: paragraphs on Maranda’s mentorship, passing the dissertation to Lévi-Strauss, and Sioui’s recollection of the endorsement.
